rationale: The service does not yet know whether young people take up peer support, whether they stay in contact, whether the role can be delivered without turnover, or whether outcomes can be measured; these are feasibility questions. A single-arm feasibility study with embedded interviews and progression criteria benchmarked on a retrieved feasibility trial (claim c2) answers them within the funded year, while designing out the role problems that drive turnover (claim c3) and focusing on first-year disengagement (claim c4).
alternatives: Randomised trial of peer support now (refused: uptake, retention and delivery in this service are unknown, and there is no trial funding)
Service evaluation without progression criteria (refused: would not tell the team whether to seek trial funding)
Interviews only (refused: cannot estimate uptake or retention)
guidelines: CONSORT extension for pilot and feasibility studies (adapted for a single-arm study)
whyNotMoreComplex: A randomised feasibility trial would halve the number offered peer support in a single service and adds little when the uncertainty is about uptake and delivery.

decision.statement: Run a single-arm feasibility study of peer support alongside the introduction of the two peer support workers in 2027, with progression criteria for uptake, retention, delivery and questionnaire completion benchmarked on the retrieved feasibility trial, and interviews with young people, families and staff.
decision.question: How should the early intervention team evaluate the introduction of peer support workers?

criteria.text: Disengagement is common and a comparable feasibility trial gives benchmarks for progression.
Peer support workers cannot be recruited or retained for the year.

gates.requirement: Funding for the peer support worker posts
gates.evidence: Innovation fund award INN-2026-31 for two posts at 0.6 whole-time equivalent from January 2027, supplied by the investigator

gates.requirement: Research and development office review and ethics determination for an evaluation that includes under-18s

decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c2 to c4 from retrieved records; the approvals gate is unknown.

summary: Feasibility study recommended; the decision rests on three ledger claims; one gate met, one unknown.
